Burst: 3 purchases of about $100 under this fingerprint within two hours
Bank model scored the transaction 0.57 (treated as a weak input: above 0.7 most alerts are legitimate)

Retrieved guidance applied: Card-not-present fraud from a new device: as card-not-present fraud, with the identity record marking the device as New for this account, sometimes behind a proxy. Stronger than plain CNP but not proof, since people buy new phones.

case.summary: The transaction of $100.09 was reviewed after the real-time model flagged it with a score of 0.57. Evidence showed the cardholder had made several similar $100 purchases on the same product and email domain, and the device profile was known, which pointed to a genuine customer. A burst of three purchases within two hours and a device-profile signal that historically correlated with fraud were noted, but the overall probability was low (5%) and the model score was considered a weak adverse input. Because the legitimate-behaviour evidence outweighed the fraud signals, the transaction was allowed and the case was closed as legitimate.
